scale: 1-10 against the bar. 8 = meets it, 9-10 = beats it, 6-7 = close with visible flaws, 4-5 = clearly below, 1-3 = broken.

elements.name: Opening wall
owns: site/js/chapters/wall.js: opening cluster and the intro load-in only
tools/bake/manifest.js: textures used only by the opening
criteria: Reads at a glance as the art bible: golden-hour plaster wall, taped memories, the name with riso 'Liew'
Name, note and chips sit in sunlight, fully legible, nothing clipped at 1920x1080
Memories cluster right of centre, at most five papers plus three stickers in view
The empty spot where the strip will land is visible and inviting, and the scroll cue says what happens next
Paper looks like paper: soft contact shadows, slight curl, tape translucent

elements.name: The flash: countdown, flash, strip prints and develops, tape
owns: site/js/chapters/wall.js: updateStrip and the flash-related camera keys
site/js/post/pipeline.js: the flash term in the composite shader only
criteria: The moment people would screen-record: 3, 2, 1, smile, then a flash that whites out with bloom, then a fresh strip slides in and develops frame by frame
Countdown numerals are big, legible, on-brand (riso pink with blue misregistration) and land where the strip will appear
The flash is HDR white with a warm bloom and recovers smoothly; no grey, flat-looking flash
The strip swings and settles like paper, frames develop top to bottom one after another, tape lands with a small press
The last frame (taped) matches the art bible composition

elements.name: About: along the wall
owns: site/js/chapters/wall.js: about cluster and the about rail keys
site/js/motion/timeline.js: blocks about-intro and about-goal, about.dolly
criteria: About copy is legible and sits in light, never on top of a photo
The camera leaves the opening cluster and arrives at the about cluster without whipping (screen speed similar to the text's scroll speed)
The about cluster (portrait, Swinburne index card, CGPA badge, coursework card, 'looking for' note) is composed like the art bible
Text and wall feel like one move, not two unrelated motions

elements.name: Transition: wall to room (light leak)
owns: site/js/app.js: plan() mix easing for wallToRoom only
criteria: Feels like warm sunlight flaring across a lens, not a white wipe
No frame is a flat white or flat beige screen; something always reads
The room is established by the end: window, beams, first card visible
Exposure ramps smoothly; no step changes between neighbouring strip frames

elements.name: Project flight: the room
criteria: Carries the golden-hour mood into a dim room: warm beams, dust, a bright far window
Each card is framed right of centre, fully in frame, big enough to read the screenshot, never overlapping the caption column (left 40%)
Cards read as real photos on paper (develop effect, tape, gloss), with depth between near and far cards
The window and beams never sit behind caption text
Camera flight slows at each card and never whips

elements.name: Project captions
owns: site/js/dom.js: project caption and counter code only
criteria: Clear hierarchy: meta line, serif title, body, stack chips, links, in the art bible's type system
Body text contrast at least 4.5:1 against what is behind it
Exactly one project caption visible at a time; the counter matches the card in view
Captions never overlap a card

elements.name: Scrapbook desk and the room-to-desk page
owns: site/js/motion/timeline.js: scrapbook, pins.scrapbook, transitions.roomToDesk, scrap-* reveals
criteria: The page sliding up reads as paper (edge, shadow), not a hard wipe
Memories drop onto the page one by one and land like paper, with the same window light as the wall
Text column legible, in light, never over a photo; at most five photos plus stickers
Feels like the art bible's scrapbook side: riso prints, tape, stickers

elements.name: Contact: the wall at dusk
owns: site/js/chapters/wall.js: contact corner, dusk light and the contact rail keys
criteria: Dusk is clearly later in the same day as the opening: same wall, lower warmer light
Email and GitHub are the clearest things on screen and obviously clickable
The last strip and 'say hi' note frame the call to action without crowding it
Ends the story: it feels like the last page, not a footer

elements.name: Chrome and type across the page
criteria: One type system everywhere: Instrument Serif display, Caveat notes, JetBrains Mono labels, Inter Tight body
Consistent margins, kicker style and spacing rhythm across chapters
Focus styles visible, links obviously links
No orphaned one-word lines in headings at 1920x1080

elements.name: Light and grain (post) across chapters
owns: site/js/post/pipeline.js: composite shader and bloom only
WALL_LOOK in wall.js, ROOM_LOOK in room.js, DESK_LOOK in desk.js
criteria: One continuous grade: warm highlights, cool-ish shadows, never orange-soaked; skin tones in photos stay natural
Bloom and halation only on true highlights (window, flash), no haze over the whole frame
Grain visible but fine; no banding in gradients (dither works)
Blacks in the room are deep but not crushed

elements.name: Phone layout
owns: the `aspect < 1` branches in wall.js, room.js and desk.js
criteria: Every screen is composed for a phone, not a squeezed desktop: name, memories and words each get their own zone
Body text at least 16px equivalent, nothing clipped, no horizontal scroll
Photos stay large enough to recognise people
Captions sit on readable backings without hiding the card

elements.name: Reduced motion
owns: the reduced-motion branches in app.js, dom.js and each chapter's stills()
criteria: No camera flights, no flash bloom, no swinging paper: each chapter is a composed still
Every piece of content is still reachable and legible
Transitions are plain cross-fades
Stills look as good as the animated version's best frame
